first.rationale: Verify the two most decision-consequential competing beliefs: whether onboarding simplification reliably restores completion/time-to-value and whether targeted pricing can create sustainable qualified revenue under competitive pressure. Current intent is a guarded standard onboarding simplification experiment because both onboarding completion and activation are declining, and inherited evidence links onboarding improvements to early adoption. Guardrails should assess account quality and downstream revenue, since easier entry can increase low-intent signups.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified onboarding result improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and raised 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current completion and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected: although it increased qualified revenue short term, verified 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive renewal. Measure qualified activation, 30-day retention, and downstream revenue quality alongside completion to ensure simplification does not merely admit lower-intent accounts.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. It is the only direction with verified evidence of improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, while directly addressing the concurrent activation and onboarding declines. Do not respond to the competitor's cut with broad promotional pricing: the verified targeted-discount cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive renewal, which conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn as a key risk during the experiment and prepare a narrowly bounded retention response for future testing rather than substituting unsustainable discounting now.
